/itinerary_variants/0/stops/0/whyOnRoute.source_en: **Jeju Port (north) is the primary cruise gateway** for vessels under 140,000 GT — and the natural origin point for the east-route circuit (Seongsan / ⟦G0⟧ / Seongeup), since all three core POIs sit within a 60–80 minute drive of this terminal. For a **bus tour with 25–40 pax**, the 30-minute post-clearance buffer is essential — large groups disembark slowly and immigration backups are common during multi-ship arrivals. The 100-bus parking capacity at Jeju Port also means the coach can be **right at the arrival hall door** (no shuttle wait), keeping the day's schedule tight. If your ship docks at Gangjeong (south) instead of here, the **southern route option of this tour** is the correct match — the drive from Gangjeong to Seongsan would consume 70+ minutes one-way, eating the day.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/0/descriptio.source_en: Your driver and English-speaking guide meet your party at the **Jeju International Passenger Terminal** (제주항 국제여객터미널, address: 191 Imhang-ro, Jeju-si — UN/LOCODE **KRCHA**), the northern coast cruise port that opened in **2015** to receive international cruise vessels. The terminal has two berths — the **Main Berth (360 m, 12 m water depth, 140,000-ton capacity)** and an **Emergency Berth (306 m, 11.5 m water depth, 85,000-ton capacity)** — handling **one cruise ship at a time**. Pickup is timed for **30 minutes after your ship's posted clearance**, absorbing immigration variance during multi-ship arrivals. The driver carries an English/Korean name placard, a printed itinerary card (with all stop times and Korean-script addresses for emergency taxi use), and the operator's 24/7 contact number. Vehicle is parked in the **100-bus parking capacity lot** adjacent to the arrival hall. Before boarding, the guide reviews the day's flow, all-aboard time, weather, and any port-day adjustments. If your guests need currency exchange (Jeju Bank), a SIM/Wi-Fi rental, or use of the multilingual tourist information center, the guide accompanies — these are all on-site within the terminal. Per **South Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports & Tourism**, **810,000 cruise tourists arrived on 414 ships in 2024** — nearly tripling the prior year — so terminal congestion is realistic on multi-ship days.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/category.source_en: UNESCO Tuff Cone — Sunrise Peak (Triple UNESCO Designation)

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/timeUsed/1.source_en: Ascent to summit deck (0.8 km / 140 m gain) — ~30 min

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/timeUsed/2.source_en: Summit views + crater rim photos — ~20 min

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/timeUsed/4.source_en: Optional haenyeo viewing at base (14:00 show; may be canceled in bad weather) — ~10 min

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/highlights.source_en: **Triple UNESCO**: World Heritage 2007-07-02 + Biosphere Reserve 2002 + Global Geopark 2010-10
**5,000 years old** — Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic eruption, magma-meets-seawater steam-explosive birth
Crater **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** (the 'stone crown')
**182 m above sea level** — 0.8 km / ~140 m gain, 60-min round trip on stone-step trail
**18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** at base — 1945 kamikaze suicide-boat shelters
**Haenyeo demonstration once daily at 14:00 (subject to bad-weather cancellation)** at the seaside cove — UNESCO Intangible 2016
**Admission updated April 2025**: Adult ₩5,000 / Youth ₩2,500 / FREE under 7 + over 65
**Closes for first Monday of each month** (occasional rest day)

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ is the main natural highlight of the east route.** The tuff cone is part of Jeju's UNESCO World Natural Heritage landscape and gives cruise guests a powerful first look at the island's volcanic coastline. The stop is placed early because it is one of Jeju's most recognizable sights and because the rim walk can be adjusted to guest fitness and weather. Guests who prefer not to climb can enjoy the base area, sea views, and photo points while others continue toward the crater viewpoint.
